Chief Executive’s Foreword 
 
The LAMA All Ireland Community & Council Awards will have four 
shortlisted nominations from Fingal in this, the 20th year of the 
awards. Over the years, Fingal initiatives have been celebrated at 
this prestigious ceremony which highlights the collaboration 
between local communities and councils. Showcasing what can be 
achieved through these partnerships is a great source of pride for 
all involved and I wish to congratulate everyone who worked on the 
Fingal entries and shortlisted nominations. This year’s award 
ceremony will not only mark the anniversary of the inaugural 
awards in 2006 but also will acknowledge 40 years of the LAMA 
Executive, and a century of the main sponsor, IPB Insurance. The 
calibre of entries to the awards each year reflects our commitment 
to investment across areas such as infrastructure, climate action, 
community and place building and wellbeing for the people of the 
county. Collaboration is a key asset in realising our core objectives 
and I would like to take the opportunity to thank all our 
stakeholders for their valuable input, experience and work on 
projects and initiatives across Fingal. The shortlisted entries for this 
year’s awards are extremely deserving and represent the diversity 
of initiatives that the council is involved with. I wish everyone the 
very best of luck at the awards ceremony on February 28th.

On January 16th, the third Fingal Age Friendly Strategy (2026-2030) 
was launched by Mayor of Fingal Cllr Tom O’Leary at County Hall. I 
was pleased to attend the event with the Chair of Fingal’s Age 
Friendly Alliance, Senan Turnbull and Fingal’s Age Friendly 
Ambassador, Terry Prone along with a host of guests and Fingal’s 
wonderful Staff Choir. We all know that Fingal boasts a vibrant, 
diverse and young population, but 21% of Fingal residents are now 
over 55 years old and this demographic shift is continuing. As an 
inclusive county, it is important to ensure people of all ages feel 
included, valued and consulted – particularly our ageing members 
of society. The Age Friendly Alliance developed the Strategy 
following a period of extensive engagement with older people, 
stakeholders, and sectoral partners. The four themes of the 
strategy are:  Health and Wellbeing, Mobility and Accessibility, Safe 
and Attractive Neighbourhoods and Information and Participation. 
These themes are of importance and relevance to us all but were 
examined especially for citizens who are older and who seek to age 
with dignity and purpose in their communities. In the strategy, 
challenges which have been identified through the consultation 
process are met with a coordinated, multi-agency Action Plan. This 
body of work represents our unwavering commitment to the Age 
Friendly Programme and will be an important reference and source 
of information and knowledge for everyone. I would like to express 
my thanks to everyone who facilitated the production of the 
strategy and would encourage you all to read it here: 
fingal-age-friendly-strategy-2026-2030.pdf 
Baldoyle is the latest community which will benefit from an 
exceptional amenity right in the heart of the locality with the 
opening of Racecourse Community Centre. 
 
 
The visually spectacular circular design gives just a hint of the assets 
which lie inside the front door - A central sports hall featuring three 
courts sits adjacent to four multi-purpose community rooms and 
externally accessible sports rooms which will be well utilised by 
local and visiting sports teams. Sustainability are accessibility are at 
the core of the design and functionality of the building which boasts 
ample bike parking, electric vehicle charging points, accessible 
parking, a rain garden and a green roof. The €10m project was fully 
funded by Fingal County Council’s Community Development, Parks 
and Green Infrastructure Departments. An Integrated Design Team 
was led by Henchion Reuter Architects and included Roughan 
O’Donovan Engineers, Matt O’Mahoney Associates, Walsh 
Associates Quantity Surveyors and Dermot Foley Landscape 
Architects. Construction was carried out by Vision Contracting. The 
project team here in Fingal, the Racecourse Community Centre 
Committee, sports clubs and the local Baldoyle community were 
very pleased to see the project come to fruition following many 
years of planning and design. The centre, conveniently located in 
Racecourse Park, will form an integral part of the fabric of the 
community of Baldoyle and will be an invaluable asset for locals and 
visitors alike.  
 
There was further good news for Active Travel in the county this 
month as Fingal County Council was awarded €33.1m for projects 
as part of €360 million in Government funding for Active Travel and 
Greenways across Ireland in 2026. Key projects to receive funding 
in Fingal include the Broadmeadow Estuary Cycle & Pedestrian 
Bridge (Malahide–Donabate), which has been allocated €12.2 
million and the Auburn Avenue to 12th Lock Walking & Cycling 
Route, which will receive €2.9 million. A further €3 million will 
progress the Seatown Roundabout to Estuary Road (Swords to 
Malahide) Scheme. The New Street Malahide Improvement 
Scheme has been allocated €1 million and €100,000 will support the 
S2M Extension (Sutton to Malahide). An additional €9.6m has been 
allocated to other priority commuter projects including the R132 
Junction Upgrades (Design Stage), the countywide Bus Stop 
Enhancement Programme, and Bus Priority / Traffic Management 
Improvements. This major investment will be hugely beneficial for 
the identified 49 walking, cycling and public realm projects, other 
priority commuter projects and additional Safe Routes to School 
(SRTS) programmes. Six Fingal schools have been included in the 
recently announced Round 4 of the SRTS programme: Coolmine 
Community School (Dublin 15), Gaelscoil Ros Eo (Rush), Scoil 
Moibhi (Skerries), Scoil Oilibhéir (Dublin 15), St. Andrew’s NS 
(Malahide) and St. Joseph’s Secondary School (Rush). This funding 
will help shape Fingal’s active future by ensuring the provision of 
infrastructure and initiatives which will make it safer and easier to 
embrace active travel solutions in our day to day lives. I look 
forward to bringing you further updates on these initiatives in the 
coming months. 
 
Best wishes, 
      
AnnMarie Farrelly

Digitisation of Housing Loans and Housing 
Allocations 
 
The work to digitise paper files within the Housing 
Directorate continues.  The Housing Loans files were 
completed in August 2025, with a total of 83,000

February 2026, with 69,650 of their paper files

facilitated by the new Housing system. 
 
Digitisation of Planning Historic Files 
 
The project to digitise the Historic Planning Files has 
been completed which converted decades of legacy 
material into fully searchable, accessible PDF 
documents. The project included the digitisation of 
63,000 
pre-1998 
microfiche-based 
planning 
applications dating back to 1963; 73,000 files from 
the legacy Alchemy system; and 10,000 paper 
planning files from 1998–2002.   
 
These files are all now securely stored in SharePoint 
for improved access and long-term preservation. 
This project has replaced outdated technologies and 
processes, provides enhanced search efficiency, and 
safeguards vital historic planning files for both staff 
and the public.

Libraries 
Opening of Donabate Library at Ballisk House 
 
 
 
The new Donabate Library at Ballisk House was 
officially opened by the Mayor of Fingal, Cllr Tom 
O’Leary, on Thursday 22nd January.  
One of the most exciting features of the new library 
is the introduction of the My Open Library service 
which is due to commence in the near future. With 
opening hours extended from 8am to 10pm, 365 
days a year, this service gives library members the 
freedom to use the space beyond normal staffed 
hours including Sundays. The opening of Donabate 
Library in Ballisk House, at a total cost of €2.4 million, 
marks the completion of phase one of a two-phase 
project. Planning for phase two — an extension to 
the building and the enhancement of its facilities will 
begin in early 2026.

Fingal County Council is aware that households in the 
Fingal area who may have received a notice to quit, 
which is also referred to as a notice of termination, 
from their landlord may be worried or unsure of 
what to do. Fingal County Council and the Dublin 
Regional Homeless Executive (DRHE) would like to 
advise anyone affected of the services that are 
available to them in these circumstances.  
 
We strongly encourage tenants residing in the 
Fingal area, who have been issued with a notice 
of termination, to contact Fingal County Council 
as soon as they receive a notice from their 
landlord. The contact details for Fingal County 
Council are provided at the bottom of this page.  
When the tenants contact Fingal County Council, staff 
in the Housing Department will take note of the 
termination date.  
 
The Council advises the tenant to refer the notice to 
Threshold, a service funded by the DRHE to provide 
a Tenancy Protection Service for private renters in 
the Dublin Region, including Fingal. Threshold can 
also be contacted directly on Freephone 1800 454 
454 or via their website www.threshold.ie which 
contains more information and advice on the validity 
of your notice.  
 
The Council’s first response will be to try to prevent 
homelessness. This includes assessing the person’s 
position on the social housing list, providing advice 
on applying for Choice Based Lettings, and advising 
the person on the level of Housing Assistance 
Payment (HAP) they may be eligible to receive. 
  
Placement in emergency accommodation will be a 
last resort if no other alternative can be identified.
